cards.claim: Training VSR models from small to large spatial sizes (easy-to-hard curriculum) achieves speedup without accuracy loss
cards.conditions: VSR models (BasicVSR-M, BasicVSR, EDVR-M) on REDS and Vimeo-90K datasets; 2 spatial stages (192×240 → 384×480 for BasicVSR; 128×160 → 256×320 for EDVR-M); full-res final stage required
cards.effect: 6.2× wall-clock speedup for BasicVSR-M, 3.1× for BasicVSR, 2.3× for EDVR-M, with maintained PSNR (±0.01 variation within noise)
cards.evidence: Quantitative experiments showing PSNR 30.90-30.93 (baseline 30.91) for BasicVSR-M and PSNR 31.54-31.62 (baseline 31.58) for BasicVSR
cards.quote: Applying multigrid training and large minibatch training to BasicVSR-M and BasicVSR achieves significant speedup (i.e., 6.2×, 3.1× for BasicVSR-M and BasicVSR, respectively) without losing accuracy.

cards.claim: Dynamic learning rate reset when changing spatial/temporal resolution is necessary to prevent accuracy loss
cards.conditions: VSR training with standard cosine annealing learning rate decay; training process divided into spatial-temporal stages
cards.effect: Prevents accuracy drop from small learning rates at larger resolution stages
cards.evidence: Paper identifies learning rate as 'the devil' when sizes change without reset; proposes restarting learning rate at large values when spatial or temporal size changes
cards.quote: Simply applying the above multigrid strategy to VSR training causes an accuracy drop. The devil is the learning rate scheduler... the learning rate in training larger spatial and temporal sizes will be smaller. The small learning rate hinders the exploration ability of the network when spatial and temporal sizes are switched to larger ones.

cards.claim: Spatial and temporal resolution dimensions should not be increased simultaneously; hierarchical scheduling (spatial cycle containing temporal cycles) is superior
cards.conditions: VSR models with correlated spatial-temporal learning; 2 spatial stages × 3 temporal stages = 6 total stages per full training run
cards.effect: Better accuracy maintenance than synchronous spatial-temporal scaling
cards.evidence: Direct comparison showing combined spatial-temporal curriculum outperforms either alone or synchronous changes
cards.quote: Moreover, our experiments suggest that directly increasing the spatial and temporal sizes at the same time leads to sub-optimal results. Thus, rather than changing them synchronously, we adopt a hierarchical design with two cycles for altering spatial and temporal sizes.

cards.claim: Learning rate should scale linearly with minibatch size increases to maintain accuracy
cards.conditions: VSR training (BasicVSR-M on REDS); minibatch size 16→64 (4× increase); linear lr scaling from 2e-4 to 8e-4 (4× increase); 300k→75k iterations
cards.effect: Maintains PSNR 30.91 vs. 30.64 (0.27 pp drop) without scaling, 30.93 (equivalent accuracy) with scaling
cards.evidence: Ablation study comparing learning rates with and without linear scaling
cards.quote: When conducting learning rate scaling, large minibatch training (with warmup) achieves comparable performance to baseline... with the linear scaled learning rate, the total gradient of large minibatch is roughly equal to that of small ones.

cards.claim: Warmup phase (linear learning rate increase from small to large) is necessary when using large minibatch training
cards.conditions: VSR training (BasicVSR-M on REDS); minibatch 64 with linear learning rate scaling; first training iterations with gradual lr increase
cards.effect: Improves PSNR from 30.81 (no warmup) to 30.91-30.93 (with warmup), preventing ~0.1pp accuracy loss
cards.evidence: Ablation study on warmup strategies showing linear warmup outperforms no warmup or constant high lr
cards.quote: Since the rapid changing of weights usually occurs in the early stages of training, we apply a warmup strategy that gradually increases the learning rate from a small value to a large one to alleviate this issue.

cards.claim: Minimum spatial resolution threshold exists below which accuracy drops significantly due to insufficient information for optical flow estimation
cards.conditions: VSR models requiring frame alignment via optical flow; very small spatial patches (e.g., 128×160 mentioned as starting point, smaller not tested)
cards.effect: Training with 'very small spatial size (e.g., 128×160) leads to a large accuracy drop'
cards.evidence: Discussion of spatial cycle design constraints; no quantitative ablation provided but stated as observed limitation
cards.quote: Intuitively, the training will be faster if the spatial size starts at smaller values. However, training with a very small spatial size (e.g., 128×160) leads to a large accuracy drop. The reason might be the unsatisfying optical flow estimation due to the insufficient information produced by such small patches.
